$comment: The STRUCTURE of each of the 17 semantic strategies: how many objects, in what
roles, where they sit, how the camera moves through them, and what the beat must
supply. Channel-independent by design -- a comparison is two things measured
against each other whatever channel is speaking.
WHY THIS IS NOT THE MONOCULTURE COMING BACK. The thing that made every channel
look the same was that the RENDERER decided the look. Here the structure decides
only the grammar: which role goes where, and which way the camera travels. Every
noun in the finished frame -- the objects, the environment, the palette, the
typeface, the specific camera moves those indices resolve to, the transitions --
comes from the channel's own Visual Identity Specification. Legal Brief's
COMPARISON and Factory Floor's COMPARISON share a sentence structure and no words.
object_slots and camera_slots are INDICES into the channel's own core_objects and
camera_language, taken modulo their length. Every strategy uses a different triple,
so two strategies on one channel never resolve to the same objects or the same

object_slots[0] is always 0, 1 or 2: the subject is drawn at full framing and has to be an object with mass. Slots 3+ are a channel's incidental objects -- markers, rules, pointers -- and appear only as supporting or context.

desk-flatlay.ground: a matte desk surface, seen square from above

courtroom.ground: the dark panelling and bench of a courtroom

map-territory.ground: a map sheet, terrain seen from altitude

archive-photo.ground: the mount board an archival print is laid on

machine-mechanism.ground: the cut plane of an assembly, drawn as a section

abstract-space.ground: an empty field with no horizon, depth carried by scale alone

urban-exterior.ground: a street surface between building faces

interior-room.ground: a room's floor and back wall, furniture implied at the edges

screen-interface.ground: the flat plane of a display, chrome implied not drawn

orbital-space.ground: open space, a star field standing in for distance

forensic-lab.ground: a stainless bench under even overhead light

hospital-ward.ground: a ward floor and curtain rail, equipment at the margins

industrial-floor.ground: a painted concrete floor with machine bases on it

evidence-board.ground: a board surface things are pinned to

corporate-interior.ground: a glazed office floor, the city implied beyond it

GEOSPATIAL_RADIUS.intent: A distance is drawn on real ground and what falls inside it becomes visible.
reasons: the extent is established before anything is said about it
the frame closes on the boundary itself
the edge holds so what it encloses can be read

repeat.note: symbolic: copies standing for the stated total, not a count of real instances

ACCUMULATION.intent: Several separate things exist at once, and together they weigh more than any one of them.
reasons: the whole surface reads as one place before anything lands on it
the pile is the point; the frame closes on it as it grows
the last one lands and the frame holds so the total is legible

TRANSFORMATION.intent: One value becomes another, and the mechanism between them is shown rather than asserted.
reasons: both states are in frame from the start so the change has somewhere to go
the camera crosses from the old state to the new one
the new state holds alone

COMPARISON.intent: Two quantities are put in the same frame at the same scale so the proportion between them is the argument.
reasons: both sides enter together; a comparison shown in sequence is not a comparison
the frame pulls back until both fit at one scale
the pair holds so the ratio can be read off

TIMELINE.intent: Things happened in an order, laid along a real axis rather than described as a list.
reasons: the axis is established before anything is placed on it
the camera travels the axis in the direction time runs
the last event lands and the whole span is in frame

CAUSE_EFFECT.intent: One thing drives another and the link between them is drawn, not implied by adjacency.
reasons: the cause is alone in frame first
the camera follows the link across to what it produced
the effect holds with the cause still visible behind it

PROCESS.intent: A sequence of stages something actually moves through, in the order it moves through them.
reasons: the first stage stands alone so the sequence has a beginning
the camera moves along the sequence at the rate the stages arrive
the finished sequence is held whole

DATA_CHART.intent: Real measured values compared against each other from a common origin.
reasons: the baseline is established before any value is drawn from it
the frame closes as the values resolve
the finished comparison holds

DOCUMENT_EVIDENCE.intent: The actual text of a rule or record, with the operative part found inside it.
reasons: the whole document is in frame so the reader knows what is being quoted from
the camera closes on the operative passage
the passage is held long enough to be read

IMAGE_EVIDENCE.intent: A real sourced image, shown because of what it proves rather than as decoration.
reasons: the image is given the frame to itself
the camera moves to the part of it that carries the claim
it holds while the claim is made

INTERFACE_SIMULATION.intent: The system's own screen, doing the thing being described, rather than a drawing of it.
reasons: the interface is square to the frame the way a screen is
the camera goes to the control being described
the result holds on screen

RELATIONSHIP.intent: Several entities and the connections that actually run between them.
reasons: the entities are placed before any link is drawn
the camera moves around the arrangement so the links read as depth not overlap
the finished network holds

BEFORE_AFTER.intent: The same frame under two conditions, with everything except the condition held constant.
reasons: the first condition is established alone
the camera crosses to the second with the framing unchanged
both are held so the difference is the only thing that moved

SCALE_COMPARISON.intent: How big a number is, set against something that gives it size.
reasons: the reference object is in frame first so the scale is honest
the frame pulls back to admit the quantity being measured
both are held at one scale

VISUAL_METAPHOR.intent: An abstract idea given physical behaviour, using objects this channel already owns.
reasons: the physical arrangement is established before it is asked to mean anything
the camera moves so the behaviour reads as behaviour
the arrangement holds in its changed state

ENUMERATION.intent: Several named things, arriving in the order they are spoken.
reasons: the frame is empty so the first item is an arrival
the camera opens out as the list grows
the finished list is held whole

CINEMATIC_STATEMENT.intent: No richer representation was available for this beat, so the frame is composed rather than filled.
reasons: one object holds the frame
the camera moves slowly enough to be felt rather than watched
the frame settles
